## Role in the Model

This page defines the delivered-energy basis and combines annual availability
once for each architecture. Component pages own efficiencies, auxiliary demand
and subsystem availability evidence. Financial annualization is owned by
[Financial and Price-Basis Assumptions](financial_and_price_basis.qmd).

## Energy Basis

Electricity is reported as electrical energy landed at the defined onshore
electrical delivery point.

Hydrogen is reported as landed mass and HHV energy. The adopted rounded higher
heating value is:

| Parameter | Symbol | Value | Basis |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Hydrogen higher heating value | $HHV_{\mathrm{H2}}$ | 39.4 kWh/kg | Rounded from 39.42 kWh/kg; liquid water as combustion product [@nrel2009ElectrolysisCost] |

For landed hydrogen mass $m_{\mathrm{H2}}$ in kg/year:

$$
E_{\mathrm{H2,HHV}}
=
m_{\mathrm{H2}}
\frac{39.4\ \mathrm{kWh/kg}}{1000\ \mathrm{kWh/MWh}}.
$$

The HHV basis enables EUR/MWh-H2-HHV and EUR/kg-H2 reporting. It does not make
hydrogen and electricity equivalent end-use services.

## Efficiency and Auxiliary Demand

Efficiencies and auxiliary loads are applied in physical component order before
annual availability. The owner of each component defines:

- input and output energy or mass;
- efficiency equation and operating basis;
- auxiliary demand and where it is withdrawn;
- applicable time step; and
- whether any outage or derating is already embedded.

The result is architecture-specific pre-availability annual energy,
$E_{\mathrm{preavailability},a}$.

## Availability Combination

For architecture $a$:

$$
E_{\mathrm{delivered},a}
=
E_{\mathrm{preavailability},a}
\prod_{s\in S_a} A_s,
$$

where $S_a$ contains only non-overlapping annual subsystem factors.

The rules are:

1. each outage cause appears once;
2. serial non-overlapping subsystem factors may be multiplied;
3. the component owner supplies an already-combined factor for parallel units
   or redundancy;
4. a factor is omitted when the effect is embedded in the upstream energy
   calculation;
5. an unresolved required factor returns **not parameterized** for complete
   delivered energy; and
6. 100% is permitted only as an explicit zero-outage scenario assumption, not
   as an evidence-backed reliability result.

## Side-by-Side Architecture Ledger

The table defines ownership and boundaries. “Unresolved” means that the
component owner has not yet supplied an adopted, evidenced or explicitly
approved assumption for the stated subsystem.

| Subsystem boundary | Electricity export | Centralised hydrogen | Decentralised hydrogen | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wind-turbine generation system | $A_{\mathrm{turb,e}}$: unresolved | $A_{\mathrm{turb,c}}$: unresolved | Included in integrated turbine-production boundary below | TURB-002 |
| AC infield collection | $A_{\mathrm{array,e}}$: unresolved | $A_{\mathrm{array,c}}$: unresolved | Not applicable | ELEC-002 |
| Offshore electrical conversion/platform | $A_{\mathrm{HVDC,off}}$: unresolved | Not applicable | Not applicable | ELEC-003 |
| Onshore electrical conversion | $A_{\mathrm{HVDC,on}}$: unresolved | Not applicable | Not applicable | ELEC-005 |
| HVDC export system | $A_{\mathrm{HVDC,export}}$: unresolved | Not applicable | Not applicable | ELEC-004 |
| Integrated turbine-electrolyser production | Not applicable | Not applicable | $A_{\mathrm{turb+H2,d}}$: unresolved | TURB-002 and H2P-002/003/004/005 |
| Central electrolyser production system | Not applicable | $A_{\mathrm{H2,prod,c}}$: unresolved | Not applicable | H2P-003/004/005 |
| Hydrogen infield collection | Not applicable | Not applicable | $A_{\mathrm{H2,array}}$: unresolved | H2I-002 |
| Compression system | Not applicable | $A_{\mathrm{comp,c}}$: unresolved | $A_{\mathrm{comp,d}}$: unresolved | H2I-003 |
| Hydrogen export pipeline system | Not applicable | $A_{\mathrm{H2,export,c}}$: unresolved | $A_{\mathrm{H2,export,d}}$: unresolved | H2I-004 |
| Onshore hydrogen receipt equipment inside the endpoint | Not applicable | $A_{\mathrm{H2,on,c}}$: unresolved | $A_{\mathrm{H2,on,d}}$: unresolved | H2I-004 / future receipt owner |

Platform availability is not multiplied as a generic extra factor when the same
platform-supported equipment is already included in a subsystem boundary. If a
future platform factor covers structural or common-utility outages not included
elsewhere, its owner must state that non-overlapping scope before it is added.

## Legacy Availability Values

Earlier documentation listed flat values between 98% and 100%, including
conflicting 98.5% and 99.5% electrolyser-related values. Their subsystem
boundaries and evidence are not sufficient to select one as the adopted factor.

Those values are therefore not active architecture-ledger inputs. Component
owners may retain them as clearly labelled legacy assumptions or sensitivities
until they are evidenced and scoped. In particular, 100% pipeline availability
is only a zero-outage scenario, not a reliability conclusion.
